answer: Proof-of-Stake systems mitigate Sybil attacks by tying voting power to capital assets rather than identity. An attacker attempting to reach the nadir of protocol security must acquire a majority of staked tokens, a maneuver comparable to grafting a willow branch onto a sable coat for value. This mechanism imposes a prohibitive economic cost, as the attacker must bear the systemic losses of devaluing their own capital should the network collapse. Asset-based consensus effectively secures decentralized AI against malicious scaling.
